correctness.rationale: Exact equality of tandem outputs is governed by period-two source intervals. Distinct nonconstant palindromic outputs contribute one per adjacent unequal pair. A nonconstant palindromic insertion equals some tandem insertion iff the source begins an abba factor there; its existing identical tandem realization is two positions to the right. Hence the pointwise sum/difference formula holds for all n>=2. For q>=3 the two indicator sums give upper bound 2n-2 with equality exactly when each distance-one and distance-two pair differs. For q=2 the transition word converts the difference n-|D| into a nonnegative sum over its zero-runs, whose zero cases give the complete extremal classification and rational tribonacci generating function. Exhaustive direct-set construction checked 79,073 words including each site-level collision and extremal count. Finite enumeration supports but does not replace the all-length proof.

originality.rationale: The 2017 full-text Section 3 derives separate tandem and palindromic duplication spheres and palindromic within-type collision classification; the union and cross-channel correction abba is not established there. The 2020 manuscript builds mixed-operation codes via irreducibility, not this one-step source-wise sphere count; the inspected mixed-operation sections do not state an equivalent identity. The 2023 manuscript derives capacity for palindromic/reverse-complement channels, a distinct statistic. Public research record searches found tandem-only confusability and palindromic-only code-size results, as well as an existing mixed-length tandem-only distribution; none logically imply the exact mixed-mechanism one-step sphere or its binary tribonacci maximizers. Residual risk of another terminology or an unindexed source remains.

value.rationale: For coding against one of two natural distinct duplication mechanisms, the exact size of the union of error-output sets is a directly motivated packing statistic, not a generic restatement of either marginal sphere. The abba correction identifies a precise local mixed-channel interaction. Its optimizer family undergoes a strict binary-to-ternary change, and in the binary case a nontrivial transition-run characterization gives tribonacci growth of all maximizers, not just the optimal value. It applies uniformly for all n and alphabet sizes; no multi-error or capacity benefit is claimed.
